note: Receiver labels are reused across hardware changes: reports and corpus entries before and after a swap both say 'lnb-c'. These boundaries are the only way to separate them. Split on capture start time, not on label.

measured.survey_active_basis: 351 probes / 2808 tunings per receiver over 23.5 h before the swap

epochs.fault: lnb-c detected 3.3x less often than lnb-d. Its +430 kHz LO offset costs only ~10% of survey score (the survey spans +/-700 kHz centred on zero and does not use receiver_centers), so the offset does not explain the deficit. The unit had a separate hardware fault.

epochs.hardware_note: Both units replaced at once and are identical to each other. Identical model does not imply identical LO: free-running crystals, no shared 10 MHz reference in the chain, so the two offsets are independent draws.
